appraisal_events.evidence: "cette première matinée fut une grande déception"; he can gather not one reason to admire her, hears her "comme j'aurais lu Phèdre", finds the declaration to Hippolyte "passée au rabot d'une mélopée uniforme", below what Œnone or Aricie would have found — having first mistaken two supporting actresses for her and admired their intonations.
appraisal_events.explanation: The long-worshipped revelation yields nothing, but the narration marks the verdict as the boy's: he had admired her colleagues in her place, and the retrospective voice will immediately show that what he could not see, the crowd could.

appraisal_events.evidence: The ticket staff, whose "choix, avancement, sort" depend on her, are absorbed in transmitting her prescriptions while nominal directors succeed one another obscurely; the house breaks into frenzied applause, and "le moment où se déchaîna cet enthousiasme du public fut, je l'ai su depuis, celui où la Berma a une de ses plus belles trouvailles".
appraisal_events.explanation: Her standing is registered publicly and institutionally — the theatre is run to her will, and the crowd's acclaim is credited by the narrator with detecting a genuine stroke of genius the trained spectator missed.

appraisal_events.evidence: At the presentation the Ambassador rises with affability, but his eyes examine the boy "avec une curiosité sagace et pour son profit, comme si j'eusse été quelque usage exotique, quelque monument instructif, ou quelque étoile en tournée" — "comme s'ils n'avaient pas reçu notification de sa mise en disponibilité".
appraisal_events.explanation: Norpois's diplomatic courtesies are exposed as automatisms surviving his own retirement, performed for his own profit, and his majesty is deflated by the double comparison to Mentor and the studious young Anacharsis.

appraisal_events.evidence: Françoise, who "avait certainement un don" for cookery, lives "dans l'effervescence de la création", choosing her cuts at the Halles "comme Michel-Ange passant huit mois dans les montagnes de Carrare", and on the day itself has "la brûlante certitude des grands créateurs" — while ordering "du jambon de Nev'York".
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator raises the servant to the rank of a great artist, and the mock-heroic scale is comic without cancelling the real competence and creative certainty he grants her, set against his own "cruelle inquiétude du chercheur".

status_effects.explanation: Measured against the sublime promised her, she delivers nothing the narrator can seize, and her supporting actresses seem to him more intelligent in their delivery.
Her standing is displayed and witnessed inside the passage: an entire theatre administration exists to obey her, careers depend on her, and the house acclaims her frenetically.

His discernment is quietly discredited: he mistakes other actresses for the star, finds nothing where genius was, applauds in order to make her play better, and ends by drinking "le vin grossier de cet enthousiasme populaire" he had meant to rise above.
He is formally presented to the Ambassador in the study before dinner, admitted for the first time to a grown, official acquaintance who rises and offers his hand.
The narration turns his gravity into habit and self-interest, a diplomat still collecting observations though the government has long since stopped employing him.
She is credited with a genuine gift and the certainty of a great creator, elevated by the Michelangelo comparison even as the elevation is played for comedy.

ambiguities: The evaluation of la Berma is doubly voiced: the negative movement belongs to the boy's failed perception, while the retrospective narrator's "je l'ai su depuis" affirms that the moment he found flat contained one of her finest inventions, so her diminishment should not be read as the narration's own verdict.
